title: SIMS: Scale-Invariant Merit-Function-Based Scalarization for Multi-Task Learning

problem.claim: Multi-task learning requires navigating trade-offs among competing objectives, commonly by reducing multi-objective optimization to a single objective through scalarization.

gap.claim: Existing merit-function-based scalarization approaches are sensitive to differing objective scales, causing optimization to favor larger-scale objectives even though Pareto-optimal solutions are invariant to positive rescaling.

contributions.claim: Proposes Scale-Invariant Merit-function-based Scalarization (SIMS) for multi-task learning.
Uses a transformation-induced merit function to produce a single objective whose optimization is invariant to loss magnitudes.
Shows that requiring scale invariance uniquely determines a logarithmic transformation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The general transformation-induced merit function preserves weak Pareto optimality and admits a smooth surrogate with controllable approximation error.
Extensive experiments on representative multi-task benchmarks report that SIMS consistently outperforms existing scalarization methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: MTL involves unavoidable trade-offs among competing objectives and is commonly formulated as scalarized multi-objective optimization.
Existing merit-function scalarization is sensitive to objective scales and may favor larger-scale objectives despite Pareto invariance under positive rescaling.
SIMS addresses scale sensitivity using a transformation-induced merit function that yields scale-invariant optimization.

The scale-invariance requirement uniquely selects a logarithmic transformation, while the resulting merit function preserves weak Pareto optimality and supports a smooth surrogate with controllable approximation error.
Experiments on representative multi-task benchmarks report consistent improvements over existing scalarization methods.

source_observation.claim: Task losses in practical MTL can differ by orders of magnitude, and existing scalarization can favor objectives with larger scales.

interpretation.claim: Scalarization methods should be evaluated for sensitivity to objective units and relative magnitudes.

application.claim: When combining heterogeneous objectives, test scale-rescaling behavior and consider scale-invariant transformations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that scale invariance is appropriate for every multi-objective application or task weighting preference.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, task configurations, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or the magnitude of the controllable approximation error.
The abstract does not describe conditions, assumptions, or proof details for the theoretical results.
